paper_id: Patil et al. - 2004 - SOLONet sub-optimal location-aided overlay network for MANETs
title: SOLONet: Sub-Optimal Location-Aided Overlay Network for MANETs
motivation: Overlay multicast in MANETs requires location info for low-latency trees, but precise location updates cause broadcast storms and overhead.
problem_framing: How to build a location-aided overlay tree without frequent precise location updates, trading optimality for reduced overhead.
key_insight: Event-based updates (node crossing cell boundary) replace continuous location broadcasts; cell centers approximate node locations.
method_signature: Cell-partitioned topology with local leaders; event-based location updates on cell boundary crossing.
evaluation_criteria: Completion time comparison between optimal tree, sub-optimal SOLONet tree, and random overlay tree across varying cell sizes and member counts.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Entire topology as one cell creates star topology, causing significant performance degradation and high collision at source.
evidence_for_taste: does not compromise the performance gains
closely matches with that of an optimal tree
Smaller cell size is not recommended if the node mobility is high
the improvement in performance is offset by an increase in the service broadcast overhead
thinking_moves: 把精确度-开销的连续变量问题，转成离散格子边界触发的事件驱动模型
承认次优解性能足够好，用近似换取可扩展性
从空间分割角度自然导出leader局部化设计
通过仿真验证'性能差距不大'来论证方案可行性
